open_obligations.what_is_open:
The dense-range Boolean operator event remains unproved.  It is enough to
prove the weaker cancellation condition
\(n^4\max\{\mu_{\mathrm{cyc}}(n,d_n),0\}/d_n^7\to0\) on every subsequence
with \(d_n\ge n^{2/5}\), but the frozen primitives do not imply that
condition.
open_obligations.obstruction:
The exact five-probability expansion has separate-witness terms of order
\(p_{n,d_n}^4\), which is of order \(d_n^8/n^4\) and therefore exceeds the
newly isolated sufficient scale \(d_n^7/n^4\) by a factor \(d_n\).
Termwise completion switchings discard the necessary signed cancellation.
The published ordinary-adjacency gap controls the walk matrix but not the
centered thresholding error, and no frozen established result supplies the
missing cancellation.  Invoking the sibling-owned open-ended question
would assume the crux.
open_obligations.attempted:
I independently reran exhaustive enumeration of all \(19{,}355\) labeled
cubic graphs on eight vertices and reproduced the exact five probabilities
and signed moment.  I then redid the fourth-trace/Markov calculation without
the stronger OEQ rate and isolated the strictly weaker sufficient condition
recorded below.  I also checked the polynomial comparison \(B=W-E\): the
adjacency spectral theorem controls \(WP_n\), whereas maximum-row,
Frobenius, and unsigned collision bounds for \(EP_n\) can still exceed
\(d_n^{7/4}\) in the upper dense range and hence do not close the theorem.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Write
\[
\mu_n^+=\max\{\mu_{\mathrm{cyc}}(n,d_n),0\}.
\]
The dense-range conclusion of \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}boolean\mbox{-}operator}\)
would follow from the strictly weaker, and exact for this fourth-moment
reduction, condition
\[
\frac{n^4\mu_n^+}{d_n^7}\longrightarrow0
\qquad\text{on every subsequence on which }d_n\ge n^{2/5}.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, by \(\mathrm{lem{:}fourth\mbox{-}trace\mbox{-}identity}\) and the
positivity of all combinatorial coefficients in that identity,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(X_{G_n}^4)
&\le 2nd_n^2+Cnd_n^4+n^4\mu_n^+,
\\
\frac{\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(X_{G_n}^4)}{d_n^7}
&\le \frac{2n}{d_n^5}+\frac{Cn}{d_n^3}
   +\frac{n^4\mu_n^+}{d_n^7}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
When \(d_n\ge n^{2/5}\), the first two terms in (2) are at most
\(2n^{-1}\) and \(Cn^{-1/5}\), respectively.  Thus (1) makes the
right-hand side tend to zero.  Since \(X_{G_n}\) is symmetric,
\(\|X_{G_n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^4\le
\operatorname{tr}(X_{G_n}^4)\); Markov's inequality therefore gives
\[
\Pr\!\left\{\|X_{G_n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}>d_n^{7/4}\right\}
\le
\frac{\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(X_{G_n}^4)}{d_n^7}
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{3}
\]
From the definitions of \(X_{G_n}\) and \(P_n\), using
\(\iota_n\iota_n^{\mathsf T}P_n=0\),
\[
B_{G_n}P_n=X_{G_n}P_n+(1-p_{n,d_n})P_n.
\tag{4}
\]
Because \(P_n\) is an orthogonal projection and \(0\le p_{n,d_n}\le1\),
(3)--(4) imply
\[
\|B_{G_n}P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le \|X_{G_n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}+1
\le 2d_n^{7/4}
\]
with probability tending to one, where the last inequality uses
\(d_n\to\infty\).  Splicing this conclusion with
\(\mathrm{thm{:}sparse\mbox{-}boolean\mbox{-}operator}\) gives the
claimed uniform event with the universal constant equal to the larger of
the sparse theorem's constant and \(2\).

The sibling-owned OEQ would imply (1), because its proposed bound yields
\[
\frac{n^4\mu_n^+}{d_n^7}
\le C_4\frac{n}{d_n^3}
\le C_4n^{-1/5}\longrightarrow0.
\]
However, neither that stronger inequality nor (1) has been proved from the
frozen primitives.  The exact eight-vertex enumeration was rerun: over all
\(19{,}355\) labeled cubic graphs it gives
\[
p=\frac{513}{553},\quad
a=\frac{475}{553},\quad
b=\frac{16771}{19355},\quad
t=\frac{15493}{19355},\quad
s=\frac{2059}{2765},
\]
and hence
\[
s-4p t+p^2(4a+2b)-3p^4
=\frac{360638638}{467595722405}.
\]
This finite identity checks the reduction but does not establish (1).

open_obligations.what_is_open:
The high-probability upper edge, and hence the unconditional matched
frontier, remains open only because the dense-range graph event in
\(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}boolean\mbox{-}operator}\) is not
established.
open_obligations.obstruction:
The lower edge, seed risk theorem, and finite compiler are already
established, but none implies that a revealed uniform simple regular graph
satisfies the required centered Boolean operator bound in the dense
subrange.  Treating that event or the four-root cancellation as a hypothesis
would assume the paper's kernel, while narrowing to \(d_n\le n^{2/5}\)
would not answer the stated all-sequence problem.
open_obligations.attempted:
I audited the synthesis from the established nodes: the deterministic rate
tends to zero, so on the operator event the compiler eventually selects the
seed procedure; the minimax definition then gives the upper edge, and
intersection with the established all-procedure converse gives the matched
event.  This closes every post-operator implication and isolates the dense
graph probability as the only missing step.
open_obligations.partial_result:
All implications after the missing graph event are closed.  Let
\[
H_n=\left\{\|B_{G_n}P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le Ld_n^{7/4}\right\}.
\]
By \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) and \(d_n\to\infty\),
\[
r_{\log}(n,d_n)
=\frac{d_n^2/n}{\log(d_n+1)}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{5}
\]
On \(H_n\), Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}seed\mbox{-}upper}\) gives a universal
\(C_0<\infty\) for which the exact worst-case risk certificate of the seed
procedure is at most \(C_0r_{\log}(n,d_n)\).  Equation (5) makes this
certificate smaller than one for all sufficiently large \(n\).  By
\(\mathrm{def{:}finite\mbox{-}compiler}\), the compiler therefore selects
the seed law and its observed-data estimator on \(H_n\); by
\(\mathrm{prop{:}finite\mbox{-}compiler}\), this is a terminating exact
procedure based only on \(G_n,Z,Y\).  The definition of \(R_2(G_n)\), whose
infimum ranges over all such procedures, then gives
\[
R_2(G_n)\le C_0r_{\log}(n,d_n)
\qquad\text{on }H_n.
\tag{6}
\]

Independently, \(\mathrm{thm{:}balanced\mbox{-}all\mbox{-}procedure\mbox{-}converse}\)
supplies a universal \(c_0>0\) and events \(L_n\) with
\(\Pr_{G_n}(L_n)\to1\) such that
\[
R_2(G_n)\ge c_0r_{\log}(n,d_n)
\qquad\text{on }L_n.
\tag{7}
\]
Consequently, if the unresolved uniform Boolean operator theorem were
proved, then \(\Pr_{G_n}(H_n)\to1\), the union bound would give
\(\Pr_{G_n}(H_n\cap L_n)\to1\), and (6)--(7) would prove the two-sided
frontier with \(c=c_0\) and \(C=C_0\).  The same event \(H_n\cap L_n\)
would also give the advertised compiler MSE guarantee.  This argument
uses exactly the fixed-schedule, arbitrary-neighborhood-interference,
endpoint-second-moment class in \(\mathrm{def{:}outcome\mbox{-}class}\),
and the converse retains every outcome-blind assignment law and every
measurable randomized estimator through \(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\mbox{-}risk}\).
The only absent premise is \(\Pr_{G_n}(H_n)\to1\) in the dense range.
